doc.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: What it takes to be a leader
summary: A leader needs desire and no alternative, the same mindset as divorce not being an option.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You’ve been a side person and then you’ve led your own groups. Sometimes I would guess more than one group at the same time. What does it take to be a leader these days?

Honestly it takes a desire. That’s the first thing. And then that same thing that we just talked about where we said I have no choice, divorce is not an option, I had no choice, that being if you really want to be a leader you have to have that same mentality. Like

there’s nothing I want to do but lead. It doesn’t mean you don’t do other sideman gigs, you do those, but you have to decide that you’re going to be, and want to be a leader. Because it’s an entirely different ballgame.

You must have a prerequisite it must be, that you have a vision for your music and this requires me to be a leader because I have an idea of what I want this music to sound like. Is that a fair statement?
